Title: Disciplineless anti-bleed card suggestion (NOT a bounce)

Messages.Author: Ector
Messages.Body:
Here's a simple card that would be great to play:

Name: Restless Guard
Type: Reaction
Cost: X blood
Only usable when a minion is attempting to bleed you for X or more.
Tap this reacting vampire. The acting minion takes X unpreventable
damage. If the acting minion will not be ready after that, the action
ends.

Looks like the card isn't overpowered (you are paying X blood to deal
X damage), and it really helps against heavy careless bleed. Currently
your prey may play Archon Investigation if you bleed for 4 or more,
but who can use lots of them? After the first one your predator is
likely to bleed with care, but even a bleed for 3 is very painful,
especially when repeated 3-4 times per turn.
Restless Guard is much less expensive than AI, and you can play
several copies. You may cycle it easily - when the last minion of your
predator bleeds for 1. Paying a lot of blood is also painful enough,
but if your predator is reckless, he could play Govern + Conditioning
for 2 blood, leaving just 1-2 blood on the vampire, so - voila! - you
prevent that bleed and punish the aggressor for just 2-3 blood. This
card favors large vampires, who can spend blood more easily, which is
definitely good. This card punishes weenie bleed decks, which is
extremely good. Finally, this cards boosts blood-denial decks, which
is also good AFAIK. What do you think?

Yours,
Ector

Firstly, there are lot of noncombat damaging and blood-draining
effects in the game, and as far as I can catch the current trend,
designers are constantly trying to enforce building decks around this
theme (look at Young Bloods, for instance). Secondly, any anti-bleed
card should bounce bleed, reduce bleed. I don't like the idea of
disciplineless bounce, and bleed reduction is good only in weenie
decks, where you can use them in multiples. Punishment is the only
remaining option. And since I prefer the reaction card to the new
master, the card cannot burn a vampire as AI does. Damage is the most
logical here.

> I don't think that *every* bit of action in a game needs to be vampire
> to vampire related. Meths do need to go at it from time to time and
> total bleed reduction is not the best answer.

I disagree here. Master card should be extremely efficient to be
playable. "Counter-like" out-of turn masters should be widely usable
to be playable. Wash and SR can cancel any master card - everyone has
master cards. DI can cancel any minion card - everyone plays them. A
master card that needs a heavy bleed to work will never be as popular
as these cards: what if nobody uses heavy bleeds on the table? A
reaction card has much better chances to become playable.

Yours,
Ector

I guess I should be more specific on this. We currently have three
major S&B archetypes with Obfuscate:

a). DOM/OBF. Strongest bleeds, great acceleration/bleed (Governs) and
bounce. Can bleed only prey, no pool gain when bleeding, very limited
combat defense.
b). DEM/OBF. Moderate bleeds, usually can bounce with Telepathic
Misdirections, but this require the third Discipline at superior.
Usually no acceleration, since The Call cannot be used to bleed.Can
bleed anyone, gains pool when bleeding (Kindred Spirits), very limited
combat defense.
c). PRE/OBF. Moderate bleeds, moderate acceleration/bleed (Enchant
Kindred), usually CANNOT bounce (there are no clans with AUS/PRE/OBF
or DOM/PRE/OBF, so it's rather difficult to find a midcap vampires
with the needed disciplines, if possible at all). Can bleed only prey,
gains pool when bleeding, wonderful combat defense (Magesty,
Staredown).

As you see, the only thing PRE/OBF is lacking to become the superior
archetype is bounce. Bounce is extremely important for any S&B deck,
since you not only avoid the pool loss yourself, but also apply the
additional pressure on your prey. Should PRE/OBF have the playable
bounce, there would be no reason of playing DOM/OBF, and the only
reason to play Kindred Spirits would be the possibility to bleed
anyone.
The same could be said about the Tumnimos/Week of Nightmares decks.
They already are very strong, usually field an army of minions, have
versatile cards that combine stealth, bleed and combat protection, and
the only thing they're lacking is bounce. Give them bounce, and you'll
have to print a bunch of new cards to stop them!

Yours,
Ector

I'd just like to jump in here and use this as an opportunity to again
agitate for nice, utilitarian, non auspex bleed reduction, rather than
all sorts of crazy, complicated master cards and counters and
whatever. This has come up before, and really, I can't see how it
could possibly hurt to create flexible, non Auspex bleed reduction
cards. For example:

Obfuscate Reduction: (mod/react) obf: +1 stealth. OBF: Reduce a bleed
by 2.
Celerity Reduction: (com/react) cel: press or manuver. CEL: Reduce a
bleed by 2.
Presence Reduction: (act/react) pre: (D) bleed at +1. PRE: Reduce a
bleed by 2.

And so on. Yes, this would devalue the currency of Telepathic Counter.
But Telepathic Counter is already pretty low on the useful ladder, and
it could easily be replaced by more useful cards (say a card like aus:
+1 intercept/AUS reduce a bleed by 1 and/or a card that costs a blood
and is aus reduce a bleed by 2/AUS bounce a bleed).

Bleed reduction is a wildly under utilized mechanic that *could* be
useful and common, but up till now has been underpowered (Telepathic
Counter, generally speaking) or just garbage (pretty much all the
other bleed reduction cards that are highly conditional and reduce a
bleed by 1). To date, a couple new reduction cards have been printed
that are actually moderately useful, both from Legacies of Blood
(Ancestor's Insight and Terra Incongnita) and the primary reason for
their usefulness is their flexibility (Ancestors doubles as +1 bleed
and Terra Incognita saves you from being bounced to), but due to the
Laibon only cost, they are not going to see much use in the long run.
But they are an interesting, and potentially good, step into the pool
that I think should be utilized.

-Peter

Actually, over the last few days, this thread has merged in my head with
the Create-A-Trophy thread. I don't quite know how I'd balance it, but
it's something like a Trophy: Indemnity that lets you bounce a bleed at
some point in the future. Which might be an interesting way of
enlivening trophies and providing disciplineless bleed bounce, all at
once.

In my head, it would be temporary (perhaps one or two bleeds, perhaps
something dependent on the size of the Red List critter you pounded, or
similar). Possibly Unique/one per Methuselah at once, possibly
restricted against who it can be bounced to - if it's a gift from
another Methuselah for your burning a vampire, maybe it's harder to
bounce to that Methuselah using it, or something, so another Trophy deck
could cause you mild problems. Possibly removed from the game on use,
so to play it repeatedly, you have to load your deck with it (unlike
Trophy: Diablerie recycling for ever and ever and ever).

It could also provide interest by making it sort of worthwhile leaving a
big bleeder out, and going after a weenie to get the bounce, rather than
just going for the big bleeder - you *want* a bleed to come get you, so
you can bounce it along. Which seems a nice trade-off of strategies,
and leaves a player still able to play their game for just a little bit
longer if you do opt for that option, which seems positive for the game.
And if you don't get a big bleeder near you, well, you just pull Trophy:
Progeny or whatever else you were playing instead.

The idea isn't terribly well fleshed out in my head, but it's something
I was thinking about.

It partly followed on from some other thoughts about bounce in plain
sight, which I'd been thinking over when writing suggestions in this
thread. Pre-emptive, visible bounce as a way of making disciplineless
bounce less of a clone of existing bounce - you have to play a master
card in advance, you have to equip with the bounce card and burn it
later, you have to recruit an ally who does the bounce for you before
exploding (but who will explode anyway, at some point), a political
action even. Which of those (if any) would be appropriate, I'm not
sure, but it's thinking about doing it in non-obvious that might lead to
a quirky card with solid potential that isn't just Deflection with a bit
of different text.

The bleed deck might well be able to plan around that, or convince
someone else to help it out ("Aw, can't you banish the guy with the
Insta-Bounce-O-Matic 5000?"), or similar. And at least some costs would
have to be paid up front (taking an action+tapping a vampire, using up a
master phase slot, pool/blood costs etc.), whether you got to use it or
not.

assessment of a good number of the variables involved, which has never
come to light in this thread until the theory ("disciplineless bounce

up.

sometimes, they can - and this also does happen - prove to be
accurate. But to that effect, experimentation/assessment is still
needed. Ruling out all possibilities (which, in this case, take the
form of costs and limitations on the hypothetical card) and then
trying to find out reasons for them to not work is absolutely contrary
to any form of design, scientific advancement or anything else that
requires reasoning to function.

in any capacity (say, in a playtest). It simply doesn't work that way.

> and just dismiss me as an opponent than think. It was very

See, that's why I wonder why I even bother. There was plenty of

See, this here is where you are getting yourself into trouble, with this
sort of overstatement of the case. Does Madness Network need to get
immediately burned at all costs? Hardly. Most of the time a Madness
network hits play, it is going to do little more than let the Malkavians
set up a more defensive position (i.e. play Madness Network, keep all
their guys untapped to block, bounce, and save the Madness Network, and
then right before it is their turn, they'll go and bleed their prey with
whoever is left untapped by then). And maybe generate some extra pool
with Victoria. In a rare occasion, it'll be used for some Out of Turn
Rotschreck Rush deck, which, really, isn't even that big of a deal. Once
per turn, someone can possibly play a super trumpy combat combo,
assuming:

-They have access to aggrivated damage.
-They have a Rotschreck in hand.
-They don't want to play another important master card that turn.
-Their OOT rush isn't chump blocked.
-Their opponent can't avoid the Rotschreck by manuvering away from
Zebulon's Claws of the Dead or Immortally Grappling/Drawing out the
Beast/Skin of Nighting/whatever the Ivory Bow. Or play Psyche/Telepathic
Tracking.

And in the worst case scenario, where the OOT Rotschreck Rush does work,
how is it any worse, really, than just getting Rushed by regular trumpy
combat?

> the most clear sign of "brokenness".

There is no ultimate necessity to burn it.

> destroy MN or lose your best vampire, this is too much for me.

How is this any different than someone rushing you with Enkidu who is
going to Draw out your Beast, Immortally Grapple you, punch you, prevent
all of your damage, Disarm and decapitate you? You can't avoid that by
burning a Master card.

> Limiting Rotshcreck to acting vampires would remove the danger and
> make the game better. This, of course, is just my opinion that can be
> wrong.

I'm assuming you mean reacting vampires, just for clarities sake. This
isn't really necessary. Rotschreck OOT Rush is such an incredibly fringe
strategy it is simply not worth the effort to worry about it. And even
when you do run into it, it is really no more effective than regular
trumpy combat, but only works once around the table. And is fragile.

> Newbies love fatties and frequently play "one-man shows".

They should learn that it isn't always such a good idea to put all their
eggs in one basket. And not just 'cause of Rotschreck. There are
*countless* cards that hose All Star Decks (Sensory Dep, Pentex
Subversion, Elder Impersonation, PTO, etc.)

themselves...

What do they do when they are Sensory Deprived? Or Pentex Subverted?

> They ask me how they could defend against it, and

> always have or that aren't always appropriate in their decks. Quite
> often the only solution is burning MN on sight.

How often are people seeing these decks? Like, I play a lot of VTES. And
have for a long time. And still, I have *never* seen a MN/Rotschreck/OOT
Rush deck in play. Ever. Like, if you have a small group (which you
might), and someone put one of these decks together and likes to
terrorize the group with it, why isn't everyone simply building decks to
foil it? Use DotB if the ag damage comes from a weapon. Use Skin of
Night. Use Psyche or Telepathic Tracking. Or simply destroy the MN. If
you see the deck coming, it is really easy to shut down.

> When everyone will
> understand that, MN decks will disappear. Wouldn't it be better to
> remove MN+ Rot combo than forcing players to burn MN on sight?

No. 'Cause you aren't actually forced to burn the MN on sight. You are
only forced to burn the MN on sight if:

A) You are relying heavily on a single important vampire.
B) You have no other way to deal with the Rotschreck.

If you fit under both these conditions, then you have an out--kill the
MN on sight. If you don't fit under both these conditions, you have an
obvious out--just don't worry about it.

I'd disagree, to an extent. Clearly, against a Rotschreck deck where
you have no other way of dealing with it, burning the MN is a top
priority. (Watch out for block/Rotschreck on that action...)

But Madness Network in the hands of a good player is rarely a card you
want to see - if nothing else, you don't want to get bled at the end of
your grand-predator's turn, have your predator untap knowing that you've
run out of bleed defence, and do it again. Most decks only have to deal
with one turn being taken against it around the table, whereas the MN
deck can have the joy of two at once.

Pretty much every mistake I've seen made with Madness Network (including
a number I've made myself) has been focusing on the actions or the
vampires taking them, and not burning the MN. "Oh, but he's not taking
any actions he couldn't have taken without it." Yeah, but it completely
screws normal expectations.

Now, if you were a super-experienced player against MN, you could
probably cope with that by modifying all your expectations
appropriately. But pretty much all of us aren't, as we only see it once
in a while.

Thus, when you next have a spare action, burning the MN is almost always
a good thing. Obviously, you may have:

- more important things to do, like picking your vampires out of torpor
before they get eaten
- a Madness Network deck being played by someone who isn't exploiting it
very well

in which case, do whatever you want, obviously. But in a general,
tournament-wide sense, I can't think of any games I've seen where
leaving Madness Network on the table with a halfway decent Methuselah
was the right strategic option.

Note that because Rotschreck is a master card, any time you can burn the
Madness Network is a master phase that has to be used to replace it. So
even if you get Rotschrecked if/when the MN player blocks[0], if you
burn it on the next action, the player can't replace it that turn
because they've used up their master phase. Of course, they can try for
the Parthenon or even Rumors of Gehenna, but the card flow is much more
precarious here anyway. And the Parthenon is subject to its own
problems, such as Arson.

>They should learn that it isn't always such a good idea to put all
>their
>eggs in one basket. And not just 'cause of Rotschreck. There are
>*countless* cards that hose All Star Decks (Sensory Dep, Pentex
>Subversion, Elder Impersonation, PTO, etc.)

Yes, this is a common problem with fatties full-stop. And Madness
Network/Rotschreck is pretty damn hot when it works, but it's so rickety
that there are lots of ways of taking it apart.

For my money, it's somewhat like the old situation with Temptation of
Greater Power, before it was downgraded. Focusing on the play of ToGP
does have places you could work - playing Sudden Reversal, for example.
Ditto Rotschreck, you can play TT, Psyche!, Tranquility, or whatever.

Instead, you can focus on the enabling pieces - such as taking out the
Justicar or, here, stopping the OOT rush being viable.

Now, I guess going against what I said above, if you have a deck-full of
TT and Psyche! (or similar), you can leave the Madness Network alone and
focus on defending against the Rotschreck with those. Although you
won't like not untapping... But yeah, you have those cards against that
deck, you could probably leave the MN alone a bit - though watch out for
the deck deciding to bleed you for 3 then 3 again instead.

If you've chosen not to use all the versatile tech that's available to
deal with this sort of thing, then your solid remaining choice is to
burn the MN. So it doesn't have to be burned quickly, but if you
haven't brought the toys with you that allow that resilience against it,
you prioritize taking it out.

motivations. Malkavian Princes turned up, for 2nd Tradition
untap/block, for good defensive card efficiency.

You are absolutely right here.

But please, everybody, let's discuss this in a separate thread that
I've just created!
It would be really great to have a chance of discussing disciplineless
antibleed cards here. Seems that I found some new arguments...

Let's look at my latest creation (based on the advice of James Coupe,
of course):

Name: Guarding the Base
Type: Reaction
Cost: 1 pool
Only usable when you are being bled. Tap this reacting minion. Choose
another Methuselah other than the controller of the acting minion. The
acting minion is now attempting to bleed that Methuselah.
Your minions cannot bleed next turn.

Would you like to play this card? I would. It's simple, it's powerful,
and it can be played even by the allies. S&B isn't going to use this
card, thanks to the last restriction, but, unfortunately, voting decks
still remain. If we add "Requires a vampire with capacity above 4"
here, the card will be disabled for weenie vote, but not for the
midcap stealth-vote. I don't think that stealth-vote needs such a
boost, but let's leave the card as is for now and discuss whether we
really need a BOUNCE card or not.

A bounce card has the following features:

A). You avoid losing pool for the bleed.
B). You can force your prey to lose pool or at least to spend some
resources (Wakes, intercept, bounce etc)
C). You can punish your bleeding predator (by ousting your prey with
his help and getting 6 pool).
D). You can allow your intercepting ally to block the action and
torporize the acting vampire.

Actually, features B and C are precious only if you can defend against
bleeds good enough (a Wall deck, for instance) or you can oust your
prey fast enough. Both types of decks need a new bleed bounce card
much less than the decks that CANNOT defend against bleeds good enough
and cannot out their prey quickly - Rush decks, for instance.
Moreover, we were trying to create a card that would be unusable in
the fast-killing decks!
Let's look at the B and C features from the Rush player's perspective.
If that player would bounce bleed to his prey, his S&B predator would
thank him for his help in ousting the next prey. The slow-killing deck
won't be able to oust his prey before his fast-killing predator ousts
him. Thus, the bounce is no "punishment" here, and S&B can bleed
without any fear.

Now please look at my Restless Guard:

Name: Restless Guard
Type: Reaction
Cost: X blood
Only usable when a minion is attempting to bleed you for X or more.
Tap this reacting vampire. The acting minion takes X unpreventable
damage. If the acting minion will not be ready after that, the action
ends.

This card has three effects: avoiding pool loss (A), punishing the
bleeder (C) and further slowing the bleeder (let's call it E), since
he will be forced to resque the bleeding vampire, hunt, and so on. As
we just saw, the most popular bounce effect (B) is not especially good
for the slow-ousting decks that cannot handle being ousted themselves.
Thus, any attempts of creating cards with this effect aren't going to
help much the decks that need the help most of all. If I would play a
Rush deck, I would definitely prefer Restless Guard to Guarding the
Base.

The only effect left is D, which can potentially result in a very
interesting cards. What about this:

Name: Hired Guard
Type: Reaction
Cost: 1 blood
Only usable when a minion is attempting to bleed you for 3 or more.
Choose a Methuselah other than you and the controller of an acting
minion. That Methuselah can tap any untapped minion he controls to
enter combat with the acting minion. If the acting minion will not be
ready after that combat, the action ends; otherwise, the chosen
Methuselah burns 1 pool.

This is surely a good "bounce" card! Two combat-heavy decks will stop
the S&B quite easily, if they deal.

Another option, certainly, is creation of a bounce card specifically
for the Rush decks (Trophy and the like). Here we can make a STRONGER
card than the traditional bounce, since the requirements are going to
be quite harsh.

What do you think about it?

Yours,
Ector

Re: face-eating.

The difficulty I've seen in play goes much like this:

- Against any "normal" deck, a player may do something like leave a
vampire untapped, leave a Wake in hand, and hold a Deflection.
Obviously, the specifics will vary from deck to deck. Three
actions taken against you, you decide how to deal with them. If
you're *really* lucky, you can maybe bounce the first bleed and
stay untapped, block, and Wake, and do something to all three.
Realistically, you might be able to choose to do something to
two actions, though.

- Against Madness Network, if you hold the same thing, you can hit maybe
two actions. Then they untap, and do it again. And you haven't
had a turn to recover. And if they're pretty confident that
you're out of defence, they can throw caution to the wind and
drop a few more bleed modifiers, happy that you're not going to
bounce.

In the turn to recover, you'd have been able to cycle your own
cards - even just tapping The Barrens again - but to defend
against six actions, how much stuff do you need to be holding in
your hand? So either you have to hold a lot more defence, or
accept the pile of damage done to you.

Now, if the MN deck isn't playing Rotschreck and isn't playing a
trick deck like Reversal of Fortunes, what with them being
Malkavians, it's pretty likely they'll have decent bleed on
hand. So a turn that might have been:

one bleed getting through,
one being bounced,
Waking and trying to do something to the third

turns into 6 actions, of which 4 get through. And these being
Malkavians, how big are those bleeds? Kindred Spirits for 2,
with Eyes of Chaos for 3, or maybe 4? Govern the Unaligned for
3?

That's a lot of pool damage to take at once, and I don't think
the vast majority of players would really know what to do in
that situation. (Hence, take the setup apart before it
happens.)
